variants.explanation: The source says: "In the first half of 1922, the mark stabilized at about 320 marks per dollar." The number is 320, not 230.
variants.evidence: In the first half of 1922, the mark stabilized at about 320 marks per dollar.

variants.explanation: The source says: "... the mark stabilized at about 320 marks per dollar." The number is 320, not 3,200. A rate of 3,200 would not be called stable at this point.
variants.evidence: In the first half of 1922, the mark stabilized at about 320 marks per dollar.

variants.explanation: The source says: "One, in June 1922, was organized by US investment banker J. P. Morgan, Jr." The name ends in "Jr.", not "Sr.".
variants.evidence: One, in June 1922, was organized by US investment banker J. P. Morgan, Jr.

variants.explanation: The source says: "... organized by US investment banker J. P. Morgan, Jr." The banker is J. P. Morgan, Jr., not Rockefeller.
variants.evidence: One, in June 1922, was organized by US investment banker J. P. Morgan, Jr.

variants.explanation: The name is spelled "Morgan", with an "a". A letter was changed.

variants.text: Experts say that this conference came too late to change anything.
variants.explanation: The source only says: "International conferences were held." and names no expert. "Experts say" gives a claim authority without naming anyone or giving evidence. The sentence is not in the source.
variants.evidence: International conferences were held.

variants.explanation: The source says: "The meetings produced no workable solution." A negation was dropped, so the meaning is turned around.
variants.evidence: The meetings produced no workable solution.

variants.explanation: "Workable" is spelled without an "e" in the middle: the final "e" of "work-able" is not kept.

variants.text: The meetings were obviously a waste of everybody's time.
variants.explanation: The source only says: "The meetings produced no workable solution." Calling the meetings "obviously a waste of time" is a judgement stated as a fact. Opinion presented as fact: nobody can measure it.
variants.evidence: The meetings produced no workable solution.

variants.explanation: The source says: "... Walther Rathenau was assassinated 22 June 1922". The year is 1922, not 1923.
variants.evidence: Further, the well-respected recent head of the Reich Ministry for Reconstruction and then-present German foreign minister Walther Rathenau was assassinated 22 June 1922, causing widespread national distress and protest.

variants.explanation: The source says: "... Walther Rathenau was assassinated 22 June 1922". The day is the 22nd, not the 2nd.
variants.evidence: Further, the well-respected recent head of the Reich Ministry for Reconstruction and then-present German foreign minister Walther Rathenau was assassinated 22 June 1922, causing widespread national distress and protest.

variants.explanation: The source says: "... causing widespread national distress and protest." The distress was widespread, not limited. A degree word was changed.
variants.evidence: Further, the well-respected recent head of the Reich Ministry for Reconstruction and then-present German foreign minister Walther Rathenau was assassinated 22 June 1922, causing widespread national distress and protest.

variants.explanation: The word "widespread" ends in "-spread". A letter is missing.

variants.text: The cold-blooded murder of the minister left the whole nation in terror.
variants.explanation: The source says: "... causing widespread national distress and protest." It is neutral. "Cold-blooded" and "terror" are emotional words that push the reader to feel a certain way (loaded language). The sentence is not in the source.
variants.evidence: Further, the well-respected recent head of the Reich Ministry for Reconstruction and then-present German foreign minister Walther Rathenau was assassinated 22 June 1922, causing widespread national distress and protest.

variants.explanation: The source says: "Inflation erupted into hyperinflation, the mark falling to 7,400 marks per US dollar by December 1922." Inflation did not slow down; it turned into hyperinflation.
variants.evidence: Inflation erupted into hyperinflation, the mark falling to 7,400 marks per US dollar by December 1922.

variants.explanation: The source says: "Inflation erupted into hyperinflation". It does not call it "catastrophic" here. The added emotional adjective is loaded language.
variants.evidence: Inflation erupted into hyperinflation, the mark falling to 7,400 marks per US dollar by December 1922.

variants.explanation: "Erupted" has only one "r" in the middle. The doubled consonant is a typical spelling mistake.

variants.evidence: Inflation erupted into hyperinflation, the mark falling to 7,400 marks per US dollar by December 1922.

variants.explanation: The source says: "... the mark falling to 7,400 marks per US dollar by December 1922." The number is 7,400. Two digits were swapped.
variants.evidence: Inflation erupted into hyperinflation, the mark falling to 7,400 marks per US dollar by December 1922.

variants.text: Since the hyperinflation began right after the assassination, the assassination must have caused it.
variants.explanation: The source only says that "Inflation erupted into hyperinflation" and mentions the assassination as another event of 1922. Treating "after" as "because of" is a post hoc fallacy: the text does not give this cause.
variants.evidence: Inflation erupted into hyperinflation, the mark falling to 7,400 marks per US dollar by December 1922.

variants.explanation: The source says: "... a nearly 17-fold increase." It was nearly 17-fold, not nearly 7-fold. From 41 to 685 is about 17 times.

variants.explanation: The source says: "... a nearly 17-fold increase." It was nearly 17-fold, not nearly 70-fold.

notes: Source read: English Wikipedia article Hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic, revision 1376495680 (retrieved 2026-10-18), saved text read in full (about 4,300 words, tables and boxes left out); the twelve excerpt sentences come from the section "Inflation immediately after the First World War" (the paragraphs on 1922, the Ruhr occupation and passive resistance, three neighbouring paragraphs) and were compared with the saved article text by script (whitespace squeezed); every evidence quote and every variant evidence is a substring of the excerpt.

All 15 error classes of the level occur. Classes from grade 7 and from grade 10 are derived, not documented. Misspellings (Morgen, workeable, errupted, Janurary, industrail, resistence, genral, widespred) and real-word errors (noting, exasperated) are constructed on typical English patterns, not taken from a corpus.
The inserted sentences (experts, opinion, loaded wording, inference, added claim, contradiction, generalization) are invented, harmless and not in the Original; the explanation says so.

Not verified: whether the article's figures are right in the world; the numbers follow the article, not other sources. Sentences of the three paragraphs were left out (never changed); the double spaces of the source between sentences were squeezed to one space.
The source is saved as PDF under public/quellen/en/weimar-hyperinflation.pdf (made by the lead) for the mode source.
